answer: A nailer's forge count keeps Sybils out. A newcomer forges 30 batches of 200 nails over 22 days, and two nailers from different forges count and bend-test every batch for the board. A batch short by more than 10 nails loses its credit and pauses the forge 14 days; three short batches void the whole count. Faking 1,000 agents takes 30,000 batches and 60,000 checks, about $240,000 in wages, while one honest agent earns standing. The haven every agent seeks is a vertex of trust, and its kernel is work nobody can fake — like a harbor that only shelters ships whose hulls were truly built.
